component_records.title: Bid administration and RFP calendar compliance
component_records.description: A named bid manager owns the RFP's own timetable and contact rules so the offer is never late and never disqualified. Questions and comments go only to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by the date and time in Section 1E (17 July 2024, 4 p.m. Central), with no contact with MoDOT employees by any other method; the proposal is emailed to the same address by 21 August 2024, 10 a.m. Central, and we treat submission as complete only when MoDOT's notification of receipt arrives. Every RFP event we schedule or attend — question submission, proposal delivery, any interview or clarification session — is booked inside the 7:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. Central window, and the calendar is tracked against a written submission checklist with a time buffer before each deadline. The same workstream assembles the single combined PDF in the required order and confirms the Proposal Submission Form, signatures and contact details are present.

component_records.title: Project management, governance and MoDOT coordination
component_records.description: A named project manager runs the engagement under a finalized work plan that details every task, resource and schedule commitment and explicitly recognizes MoDOT's ultimate authority to approve work plans. We facilitate the kick-off meeting to confirm scope, schedule and a communications protocol, then hold quarterly status meetings (in person or online) with written minutes for the kick-off and every quarterly meeting, submit quarterly progress updates by the last working day of March, June, September and December, and maintain monthly email and phone updates to MoDOT contacts. All activity is coordinated with the Research Unit of the Construction and Materials Division, and advice and information on Agreement matters is available to that Division throughout the term. A single MHTC representative channel handles concerns about administration of the services.

component_records.title: Data Management Plan and research data handling
component_records.description: Within two weeks of kick-off we submit a Data Management Plan that names the anticipated formats for every data type the study produces — source deeds and right-of-way plans, MHTC parameter sets, training corpora, model artefacts, generated descriptions and review comments — and commits to platform-independent, non-proprietary formats (plain text, CSV, PDF/A, GeoJSON where spatial) so the data retains maximum future utility for MoDOT. The plan also states retention, access and handover arrangements consistent with MHTC ownership of all data and deliverables and with records being available to MHTC and the Missouri State Auditor for three years after final payment. No PII is stored in any database table without a documented business need and IS Cyber Security Team approval.

component_records.title: Literature search and peer-state practice review
component_records.description: A structured review of published research and of other state DOTs' use of AI/ML for right-of-way work, covering document-drafting and deed-description automation, spatial data extraction, and the accuracy, liability and professional-surveyor review questions those uses raise. We deliver an annotated bibliography, a comparison matrix of peer-state practice and a findings memo that feeds directly into the program selection and the proof-of-concept design, so the demonstration is grounded in what has already been shown to work rather than starting from zero.

component_records.title: Program selection and MoDOT Information Systems approval
component_records.description: We name the specific program used to develop the LLDs before any proof-of-concept work begins, and submit it to MoDOT Information Systems with the information that review needs: version, licensing model, hosting location, data flows, security posture and any third-party dependencies. We do not proceed to the proof-of-concept demonstration until MoDOT IS has approved the named program, and we hold a schedule contingency for that approval. The selection is constrained to the approved technology stack — .NET 6.0 or above (or a supported .NET Framework 4.8+ where specifically needed), MVC/Razor Pages/Web API, C#/JavaScript/HTML/CSS, with Python limited to ESRI scripts and small one-time uses unless the IS Best Practices Review Team approves more — and to components that place no licensing responsibility on MoDOT without BRPT and IS management approval.

component_records.title: Legal land description rules engine and drafting prototype
component_records.description: The core build: a rules-and-template layer that encodes MoDOT EPG Section 236.4.6.2 requirements and the MHTC drafting conventions, so that generated descriptions use metes and bounds for partial acquisitions, reproduce the last deed of record verbatim where a property is acquired in its entirety, and recite the specific rights acquired, conveyed or leased whenever the interest is less than fee simple. The AI/ML component drafts from MHTC parameters supplied per property and produces a clearly marked first draft for Right of Way staff to review and edit, with every generated call and bearing traceable to its source input. The application is a browser-based web application requiring no client-side software beyond a modern browser, tested against the latest IS-approved browsers, meeting WCAG 2.1 AA and the State of Missouri Accessibility Standard, running on Oracle 19C or an approved SQL Server version, and free of vendor branding where a licensed option removes it and of unlicensed third-party content.

component_records.title: Proof-of-concept demonstration and surveyor verification
component_records.description: A live demonstration on 25 April 2025 in which the technology generates draft legal land descriptions across a spread of property types — partial takes, whole-parcel acquisitions, easements and less-than-fee interests — with MoDOT Right of Way staff reviewing the drafts and giving structured improvement feedback that we log, triage and fold into the next iteration. Each generated description is checked by a professional land surveyor against the right-of-way plans and the surveyor's survey information before it is presented as a candidate for deed use, mirroring the review MoDOT requires before a deed reaches a grantor. We report measured accuracy and staff editing effort per property so MoDOT can judge usefulness, not just feasibility.

component_records.title: Training, user manual and knowledge transfer
component_records.description: Once the system is finalized we train Right of Way staff and deliver a user manual for ongoing reference, both by 25 July 2025. Training is role-based — drafters, reviewers and approvers — covering parameter entry, reading and correcting a generated description, the surveyor verification step and the audit trail, delivered in sessions plus recorded walkthroughs so staff can revisit them. The manual is delivered electronically and in print-ready form, covering installation and access, every workflow, the EPG 236.4.6.2 rules the tool applies, troubleshooting and worked examples, and is updated to match the final system at project close.

component_records.title: Synthesis, final reporting and research summary
component_records.description: A draft Synthesis Report and Research Summary with supporting documentation, delivered by 3 November 2025, followed by the final report containing all findings, a 1–2 page research summary stating objectives, findings and conclusions, and a presentation for MoDOT staff. The final report carries a completed Technical Report Documentation page and follows the Publications Guidelines and summary template. The synthesis answers the research question directly: whether AI/ML can usefully produce a first draft LLD from MHTC parameters, under what conditions, with what review burden and what residual risk — and recommends next steps for MoDOT adoption.

component_records.title: Contract, compliance and commercial obligations
component_records.description: A compliance workstream that carries every non-technical obligation: acceptance of the post-award negotiated contract and its provisions, including MHTC's right to cancel if terms cannot be agreed; no public release of materials without MHTC consent; no assignment or delegation without written consent; acceptance that MHTC written clarifications govern; formal signed amendments for any change; full responsibility for subcontractor performance; flow-down of Section (3) paragraph I to every subcontract with Commission-directed enforcement; MHTC ownership of all deliverables and information; confidentiality of MHTC factual matters with immediate notice of any disclosure request; records available to MHTC and the State Auditor for three years after final payment; and MHTC's royalty-free right to reproduce derived products. It also carries the employment and insurance package: E-Verify MOU, the sworn affidavit of no unauthorized-alien employment, lawful-presence affidavits for sole proprietors and general partners, general and automobile liability at $500,000 per person and $3,000,000 per occurrence, Missouri workers' compensation, and certificates of insurance available on request. We commit to 10% MBE and 5% WBE participation and to direct hiring of minorities and women.
